accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE NC 2013 English Appendix 2 (Year 6: semi-colon, colon and dash to mark the boundary between independent clauses, 'It's raining; I'm fed up') and its glossary, the STA KS2 GPS test framework, and Cutts' Oxford Guide to Plain English: semi-colon for related clauses of equal weight, colon when the second clause explains or expands the first, dash as the informal equivalent, small letter after the mark in British English. Every lab sentence was checked: each 'correct' one has an independent clause on both sides.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors in KS2 writing and GPS marking: the comma splice (comma tile and splice fixes refused), a semi-colon before a subordinate clause or phrase ('I was tired; because I ran all day', 'After lunch; we played outside'), keeping 'and' after a semi-colon (challenge), colon versus semi-colon confusion (explains versus balanced sort), and the dash used for list items (challenge).

lab_distinct.evidence: The scenes work on this topic's own mechanism, the clause boundary: the learner taps the exact gap where the first independent clause ends in run-on sentences, and each wrong gap is explained as 'not a full clause yet' or 'runs past the end'; the cover test judges each side of a mark; the splice scene picks every valid fix. It could not be reused for another grammar point by relabelling.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the boundary before the mark is offered, sees the comma rejected as a splice and the joined sentence written out with its semi-colon, discovers the explain-versus-balance difference from six sentences, and applies the cover test before the done text states it. Done messages sum up the rule only after each task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Yes, it has a verb' for 'because it snowed' (it sorts only into Cannot stand alone), 'Yes, a comma is a short pause' (the comma tile is refused as a comma splice) and 'A semi-colon' for the bike-by-the-door sentence (it sorts into Colon: explains).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; wrong options are tagged splice, join, cover, colon or dash, each with its own message, such as 'A semi-colon replaces the joining word. Do not use both' and 'It is not used to separate list items'. Lab misses name the slip too: 'With no mark the clauses run together into a run-on sentence.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs define independent clause with an example and a non-example, then give one example sentence per mark with its job in plain words; validate_lessons readability passes for kid and adult text. Canvas text uses short sentences children can read in one go, and the bins say the rule ('Colon: explains', 'Semi-colon: balanced').

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence gives a rule, an example or the test; the adult paragraphs give the curriculum statement and key words, each mark's job, the common mistakes and what each lab scene does. The content gate finds no filler phrases.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark. Sentence cards wrap inside 2-column tiles; in the boundary scene the first shot wrapped one word onto its own line, so word chips now shrink to fit and each row is centred, with grey dots marking every tappable gap and the chosen gap shown as a blue bar; mark tiles are 64 px tall; the five splice versions fill the width at 14 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'The bus was late → Stands alone', 'Boundary after "raining"', 'Use a semi-colon (;)', 'Use no mark' and 'Fixes it: It was cold. We wore coats.' The canvas aria-label updates with each message, challenge feedback is a polite live region, and the walk gate's axe check is clean in both themes.
